newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian Marxists seek change to car incentive law.
newsitem.headline: Italian Marxists seek change to car incentive law.

text.p: The government must draw money for a car incentive scheme from a different state fund than the one presently earmarked, government ally the Communist Refoundation said on Monday.

Prime Minister Romano Prodi introduced incentives at the start of the year encouraging motorists to trade in ageing cars for new ones. He said he would take the necessary cash from a fund set aside for 'socially useful labour projects'.
Refoundation, which holds the balance of power in the lower house of parliament, said it would introduce an amendment stipulating that the money must come from a special prime ministerial fund.
Refoundation senator, Leonardo Caponi, who is head of the upper house industry commission, said that if this amendment was approved, the party would vote for incentive measures.
The government scheme, which offers motorists up to two million lire ($1,300) for swapping in cars over 10 years old, was introduced by a decree law and has to be approved by parliament.
